study_identification_part.si_4_title: Charting brain growth and aging at high spatial precision

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study employed a warped Bayesian linear regression (WBLR) model. Specifically, they used Bayesian Linear Regression with likelihood warping (using a 'sinarcsinsh' warping function, equivalent to the SHASH distribution) to model non-linear and non-Gaussian effects. The modeling was implemented using the PCNtoolkit package (version 0.20).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We employed a warped Bayesian linear regression model to accurately model non-linear and non-Gaussian effects... Normative modeling was run using python 3.8 and the PCNtoolkit package (version 0.20). Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) with likelihood warping was used... We employed a 'sinarcsinsh' warping function
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Rutherford2022.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Normative modeling

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled cortical thickness (CT) and subcortical volumes (SubV) derived from Freesurfer (version 6.0) using the Destrieux parcellation. They also modeled global features such as mean cortical thickness across the entire cortex and total gray matter volume (GMV).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: fit normative models for cortical thickness and subcortical volume derived from Freesurfer (version 6.0)... sex differences between females (red) and males (blue) are most pronounced when modeling large-scale features such as mean cortical thickness across the entire cortex or total gray matter volume.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models were fit using a set of covariates: age, sex, and fixed effects for site. Age was modeled using a B-spline basis expansion (cubic spline with five evenly spaced knots) to capture nonlinear effects.
